summary: Somalia requires every foreign visitor to hold an electronic authorisation (E-Visa/ETAS) obtained at etas.gov.so before departure — the Immigration and Citizenship Agency launched it on 1 September 2025 in place of applying on arrival. The self-declared Republic of Somaliland runs its own, entirely separate entry regime.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says that to enter Somalia, including Somaliland, your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive.

source.name: UK FCDO — Somalia travel advice: entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement: WHO's country list and CDC both state Somalia does not require proof of yellow fever vaccination. WHO and CDC generally do not recommend the vaccine, except that it may be considered for the southern regions (Bakool, Banaadir, Bay, Galguduud, Gedo, Hiiraan, Lower and Middle Juba, Lower and Middle Shabelle).

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health: country list of vaccination requirements (2022, revised 2023)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: The CDC says malaria is present in Somalia and recommends that travellers take prescription medicine to prevent it, starting before the trip and continuing during and after it.

source.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Travelers' health: Somalia

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for Somalia. The UK Foreign Office advises having travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover medical treatment, evacuation by air ambulance and repatriation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Somalia travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: The US State Department warns that travellers arriving in Somalia without an onward ticket or a clear reason for travel may be refused entry. No Somali source we could read states the rule.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Somalia international travel information

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Somalia.

source.name: Immigration and Citizenship Agency of Somalia — Our services: visa services and their requirements (no funds requirement listed)

currencyLimits.text: In Somaliland, cash or travellers cheques worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared. No official threshold is published for the rest of Somalia.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Somalia travel advice: entry requirements

notes: The UK FCDO says drinking and selling alcohol is banned in Somalia.

The UK FCDO says khat is legal in Somalia but taking it out of the country is an offence; bags are regularly searched at Hargeisa and Mogadishu airports, and anyone found with khat is likely to be prosecuted.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted in Somalia and you cannot get cash advances on them, so take cash with you; the US dollar is the main currency for exchange. Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and that ATMs, where they exist, are in major cities, usually in hotels, malls and other secure areas.

safety.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except the Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil regions, where it advises against all but essential travel; Canada advises avoiding all travel. The FCDO says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks, including on hotels and Mogadishu International Airport, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping throughout the country, including Somaliland.

tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil, where it advises against all but essential travel; Canada advises avoiding all travel. The FCDO says road travel is dangerous and to get advice from a security firm or sponsoring organisation.

The UK FCDO says that if you fly to Hargeisa you may be asked to show the Somali eVisa to board, but it is not valid for entry there: you must buy a single-entry visa on arrival at Hargeisa International Airport, valid for one month.

The E-Visa/ETAS has been required of all foreign nationals since 1 September 2025 and is applied for before departure, not on arrival. The Immigration and Citizenship Agency encourages applying well ahead of travel, relying only on etas.gov.so, and keeping a copy of the approval to present on arrival.

Take cash, in US dollars: the UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted and the dollar is the main currency for exchange. In Hargeisa you can withdraw dollars from ATMs with international cards.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Somalia?
faq.answer: Yes — every foreign visitor needs one. Since 1 September 2025 Somalia's Immigration and Citizenship Agency requires all foreign nationals to apply for their E-Visa/ETAS online at etas.gov.so before the journey rather than on arrival. No official source publishes the fee; it is paid with the online application.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Somalia?
faq.answer: No. The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except three north-western regions (Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil), and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks; Canada advises avoiding all travel. FCDO support is severely limited, with no in-person consular help.

faq.question: Is Somaliland's visa different from Somalia's?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK FCDO says the Somali eVisa is not valid for entry at Hargeisa: travellers flying in must buy a single-entry Somaliland visa on arrival, valid for one month, although airlines may still ask to see the eVisa at boarding.

faq.question: Can I pay for the Somali visa on arrival in cash?
faq.answer: Not according to any official source. Since 1 September 2025 the Immigration and Citizenship Agency requires every foreign national to obtain the E-Visa/ETAS online before travelling, and the fee is paid with the online application. No official page publishes a visa-on-arrival fee.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Somalia?
faq.answer: No. WHO's country list and CDC both state Somalia does not require a yellow fever certificate for entry.
